mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.0% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in the current month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprise in a restrictive policy phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-increase average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.0% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a policy rate hike, which elevates risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for at least two consecutive months
regime_hint: Escalating inflation expectations in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 30-day pre-inflation-spike average (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL never exceeds 0.3% in the following 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of more than 50,000 suggests labor market slack, which can precede a softening economic cycle and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 in the current month
regime_hint: Early-stage labor market loosening before recession
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative compared to the 30-day pre-increase average (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS does not exceed the threshold in two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (retail sales) and RSAFS (federal reserve balance sheet) simultaneously increase by at least 2% month-over-month, it signals resilient consumer and liquidity demand, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥2% and RSAFS increases by ≥2% in the same month
regime_hint: Concurrent strength in consumption and liquidity indicators
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the 30-day pre-signal average (t-test p > 0.05), or either proxy falls below threshold in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side momentum, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by ≥3% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Prolonged softening in US industrial production
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative compared to the 30-day pre-triple-consecutive-decline average (t-test p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% for two consecutive months is interpreted by markets as a labor market tightening, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market tightening before wage growth
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive compared to the 30-day pre-drop average (t-test p > 0.05), or UNRATE does not fall below 4.5% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are rising but FEDFUNDS outpaces CPIAUCSL by at least 0.2 percentage points monthly, the market anticipates continued monetary easing, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥0.2pp more than CPIAUCSL for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Relative easing (FEDFUNDS-CPIAUCSL gap widening) in a low-inflation environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the 30-day pre-gap-widening average (t-test p > 0.05), or the gap reversal occurs within the next 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP chain-weighted personal consumption) of at least 2% while HOUST remains flat or rising indicates a shift from consumption to investment demand, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% for two consecutive months and HOUST does not decline
regime_hint: Transition from consumption-led to investment-driven growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative compared to the 30-day pre-signal average (t-test p > 0.05), or GDPC1 recovers in the following quarter without a sustained investment demand signal.
